summary: Train in food insecurity analysis, shock assessment and anticipatory action. Build practical assessment and briefing skills. Explore the course.
lede: Food security and agricultural resilience analysis uses household, market and hazard evidence to assess risks and guide response planning. For food security analysts, agricultural resilience practitioners and programme staff, the course develops practical skills for turning this evidence into assessments and early-warning outputs. Participants practise checking data quality, comparing indicators, interpreting livelihood shocks and resilience evidence, and preparing maps, briefs and response-planning inputs.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who collect, analyse or act on food insecurity and agricultural shock evidence. It suits intermediate practitioners who contribute to assessments, early warning, programme decisions or resilience monitoring.
audience: Early Warning and Anticipatory Action Officers
Food Security Programme Officers using assessments
modules: Classification with the IPC Technical Manual
prerequisites: Prior experience collecting or interpreting food-security, agricultural-livelihood, market, household or hazard evidence is expected. No programming is required.
